Investment Analyst, 25 October 2026. All money in SEK. Bases, sources and definitions are in the end notes.

#0. Summary: the key insights, implications and conclusions

The investment case in one sentence. Avanza, a top-decile franchise, is entering the weakest eighteen months of its five-year earnings path; consensus estimates have not yet adjusted to that trough, but the share price's multiple already has, so the case is about when to buy rather than whether, and the dated events that decide the timing fall between 4 November 2026 and 16 April 2027.
The implication for Richard: prepare the position now and size it after the estimates reset on 22 January 2027. Three facts set this timing. The skew of fundamental outcomes is positive over 12 to 24 months. The skew of estimate revisions is negative for the next two quarterly reports. The share price already sits at a fair trough band. Waiting until 22 January could cost 5% to 10% of upside if the Riksbank decision and the January cost guide both land well. Waiting also avoids the one event that could take the shares to SEK 310 to 330: a Q4 miss against estimates that have not yet been cut.

The business. Avanza is the strongest consumer financial franchise in Sweden and one of the strongest in European financials on every static measure.

Avanza's moat is built on sharing its scale with customers: each year of growth lowers the cost per customer, Avanza passes the saving on, and the moat widens. The same promise is the reason Avanza's unit prices never rise.

The five insights that matter.

  1. Q3 2026 split Avanza's asset growth from its income growth, and about two-thirds of the split is permanent.

    Savings capital grew 21% year on year in Q3 2026, but operating income grew only 12%, because every unit yield fell. The brokerage yield fell to 10.3 basis points of turnover (from 11.0), the fund margin to 22.2 basis points (from 22.9) and the blended currency margin to 18 basis points (from 19). Annualised income per customer fell 6% in a single quarter, to SEK 2,170.

    Management calls the yield decline "temporary market sentiment". My reading, which the second and third analysis sets share, is that about two-thirds of the decline is structural, because it comes from the customer and product mix that Avanza's own strategy deliberately builds: affluent customers now account for 30% of trading and pay half-price currency conversion; index funds hold 55.5% of fund capital; and Sigma, the new private-banking offer, is priced at half the incumbent banks' price.

    Avanza's revenue margin on savings capital therefore drifts down from 44 basis points in FY2025 to about 42 in 2027 and 38 by 2030. Savings capital must grow 11% to 12% a year for revenue to grow 8%. The franchise is intact; the rate at which it converts assets into earnings has reset lower.

  2. 2027 is the trough year of Avanza's earnings path, and consensus has not yet priced the trough.

    In 2027 revenue grows about 8% while costs grow 13%: the 8% annual cost growth of Avanza's Swedish cost framework, plus a Danish expansion bill that steps up from SEK 40m to about SEK 130m. Operating profit therefore grows only 6%, and the operating margin falls 1.3 points to 68.2%.

    Consensus still holds the 2027 operating margin at 69.5% and FY2027 EPS at SEK 20.87 (median; the mean is SEK 21.1). Consensus did not move after a Q3 operating profit miss of 2% in which every revenue line came in below expectations. Our base of SEK 20.2 is 3% below consensus; DNB Carnegie's SEK 19.3 is 7% below. Only three of the thirteen houses have published since the Q3 report.

    I expect the next two revision rounds to cut estimates: the Q4 consensus compilation in mid-January and the Q4 report on 22 January should together take FY2027 consensus EPS down 2% to 4% and FY2028 down 3% to 6%.

  3. The share price has absorbed more of the bear case than the estimates have.

    At 16.2x current earnings, the shares sit at the 12th percentile of their own ten-year range. At 17.2x two-year-forward earnings, they sit at the 5th percentile of the last two years. Avanza trades 3 turns below Nordnet (19.3x) and only a turn above the sector median (15.2x), although the sector's return on equity is ten points lower than Avanza's.

    A fair trough price for the shares is SEK 310 to 345, 4% to 14% below today's price; the 52-week low is SEK 307. The downside from a lower multiple is therefore small. The larger downside sits in earnings: a 2022-type activity year would cut EPS 20% below our base, and Avanza's operating leverage would pass the full revenue fall through to profit because its costs do not flex.

  4. The skew of fundamental outcomes is better than the skew of near-term estimate revisions, and the two skews cross in the spring of 2027.

    Four levers favour the case, and the estimates carry none of them as a positive:

    • The policy rate is now an asymmetric lever. The Riksbank has turned from a two-year headwind into a two-sided lever that skews positive for Avanza's earnings: each point of rate hikes adds SEK 1.1bn of pre-tax profit a year, while each point of cuts costs SEK 420m. Avanza's own deposit beta of 36% in 2023 says that the base case's assumption of 60% to 70% pass-through to customers of the expected 4 November hike is conservative.
    • The capital constraint is loosening. The leverage ratio has moved from binding (4.2% in March 2026) to loosening (4.8% in September) and should reach 5.2% to 5.5% by 2028, which makes a first share buyback an option in 2028.
    • Denmark is unpriced. The Danish launch in H2 2027 is in the estimates in neither direction.
    • The Swedish risk tax is out of reach. Some commentary carries the Swedish risk tax on credit institutions as a 2029 cost, but the tax does not apply inside our four-year forecast range: its threshold is SEK 197bn of liabilities, against Avanza's SEK 114bn.

    Q1 2027, reported on 16 April, is the first quarter with a full quarter of the higher policy rate and an easy cost comparison, which makes it the likeliest earnings beat of the horizon.

  5. The return is a call on the multiple, and Viewforth's guideline fair multiple overstates it.

    On our base, two-year-forward EPS rolls from SEK 20.9 today to SEK 23.3 at end-2027 (+12%) and to about SEK 26.3 by mid-2029 (+26%), and dividends add 4% a year. If today's 17.25x multiple simply holds, the shares return 13% a year with no help from a re-rating.

    Viewforth's guideline fair multiple of 22.15x, set by its Phases page at the 60th percentile of the stock's ten-year range for a "Turning/Inflecting" phase, would add 28% on top of that return. The model's one-page summary used an older guideline of 27.70x and shows +77% to December 2027, a return that belongs to a phase the stock is not in.

    My fair multiple is 19.5x for the next 6 to 18 months: the stock is stalling on earnings and turning on assets, and 19.5x sits in the upper half of the stock's multiple range since 2022. My fair multiple rises toward 21x by 2029 if income per customer stabilises above SEK 2,100 and the Danish launch lands on budget. At 19.5x the total return is about +30% to end-2027 and +55% to mid-2029 (18% a year). Weighting in a 25%-probability bear case gives a probability-weighted return of about +25% to end-2027.

The single number to watch is income per customer. Above SEK 2,300 a year, the activity cycle is back and the bull case is live. Below SEK 2,050, the forces that cap Avanza's yield have won and the base case needs cutting.

The four judgements that move the value of the shares, with the arithmetic

The pointTwo judgements move the value of the shares far more than the others: trading velocity, which swings FY2027 EPS between +7.5% and -20%, and the fair multiple, which is worth 17% of the share price. The revenue margin and the policy rate matter at about 5% of EPS each; the cost line barely registers.

Conversion rules used in the arithmetic below: 2027 average savings capital is SEK 1,340bn; 90% of costs are fixed within the year; the tax rate is 14.5%; there are 158.8m shares. SEK 100m of pre-tax profit is therefore SEK 0.54 of EPS, or 2.7% of the FY2027 base EPS of SEK 20.2. Each turn of the two-year-forward multiple on FY2029 EPS of SEK 23.3 is worth SEK 23.3 of share price, or 6.5% of SEK 360.

Judgement 1: how much of the Q3 yield compression is structural, which sets the revenue margin path.
Base
A revenue margin of 41.8 basis points on average savings capital in 2027, drifting down 1.2 basis points a year.
If cyclical
The margin holds at about 43.3 basis points, the level consensus implies. Revenue rises SEK 200m and operating profit SEK 180m (after a little variable cost); EPS rises SEK 0.97, or 4.8%, to about SEK 21.2; the 2027 operating margin is 69.3% rather than 68.2%.
If fully structural
The margin drifts 2 basis points a year, as it did from 2023 to 2025, to about 40.5 basis points. Revenue falls SEK 175m; EPS falls SEK 0.85, or 4.2%, to about SEK 19.4, which is DNB Carnegie's estimate.
Worth
Plus or minus 5% of 2027 EPS.
Decided by
The brokerage yield, the fund margin and income per customer reported on 22 January and 16 April 2027.
Judgement 2: trading velocity, which drives brokerage and currency income (SEK 2,160m in the 2027 base, 39% of revenue).
Base
Turnover per customer at 90% of the 2026 average, an average that included the H1 2026 peak.
If H1 2026 velocity returns
Revenue rises SEK 290m and EPS SEK 1.5, or 7.5%. Combined with a second rate hike and stable deposits, this is the SEK 22.5 bull case (+11%).
If 2027 is a 2022-type year
Transactional income falls 25%, markets fall 15%, fund capital is flat and deposits rise as a partial cushion. Revenue falls to about SEK 4,800m while costs stay at SEK 1,750m, so operating profit is about SEK 3,050m and EPS about SEK 16.2: 20% below the base and 15% below the prior year. At a trough multiple of 15.9x on the correspondingly lower forward EPS, the share price would be near SEK 300.
Probability
About 25% for each tail. Trading velocity is the largest single source of forecast error in both directions.
Judgement 3: the policy rate and deposits, which drive net interest income (SEK 2,130m in the 2027 base).
Base
One 25 basis point hike on 4 November, passed through to customers at 60% to 70% (worth about SEK 160m a year), and a three-month Stockholm Interbank Offered Rate (STIBOR) of 2.25%.
Second hike by February 2027
Nordea's call, with perhaps a 40% probability: +SEK 100m of pre-tax profit in 2027, +SEK 0.54 of EPS, +2.7%.
No hike in November
A minority view: -SEK 160m to 200m, -SEK 0.9 to 1.1 of EPS, -4.5% to -5.5%. A November hold is the one event that would turn the whole peer group's estimate revisions negative at once.
A full point of cuts
The recession tail for 2027 to 2028: -SEK 420m, -SEK 2.3 of EPS, -11%.
Deposits
Deposits rebuilding to 9.5% of savings capital in a risk-off winter add SEK 50m to 100m (+1% to +2.7%); deposits falling to 8% subtract the same.
Decided by
The realised deposit beta sets the magnitude, not the sensitivity Avanza publishes.
Judgement 4: the fair multiple, which is worth more than any earnings judgement.

The gap between my fair multiple (19.5x) and Viewforth's guideline (22.15x) is 2.65 turns of FY2029 EPS: SEK 62 a share, or 17% of the current price. The gap turns on whether the market reads 2027 as a stalling year (my base) or as the first year of a new growth leg (Denmark, a second hike and trading velocity returning). The dated evidence for either reading arrives in H1 2027.

The cost line, by contrast, is not a judgement that moves the shares. Each point of Swedish cost growth is SEK 16m (SEK 0.09 of EPS, 0.4%), and a SEK 50m Danish overrun is SEK 0.27 of EPS (1.3%). Four years of cost guides met or beaten say that the error on costs is small and, if anything, favourable.

#1. Operating environment: tailwinds, headwinds and risks

The pointThe external forces support Avanza's volume lines with high confidence, but the market is pricing the fast, cyclical headwinds on trading activity and yield, and the external picture supports neither a return of H1 2026 trading velocity nor a sector re-rating.

Evidence: the structural tailwind accelerated in 2026. Swedish households are moving savings from banks to digital platforms, and the shift sped up this year. Avanza's share of Swedish savings capital rose from 7.8% at end-2024 to 8.7% in September 2026. Its 11.9% share of market inflows is above its share of the stock of savings, which is the signature of continuing share gain. Avanza took 32% of all Swedish fund inflows in Q3, a record SEK 18bn. Net inflows of SEK 23.1bn were up 61% year on year, and two-thirds came from existing customers, who still keep two-thirds of their wealth elsewhere.

Evidence: regulation and the rate cycle have turned supportive. The tax-free threshold of the investment savings account (ISK) doubled to SEK 300,000 in January 2026. The EU Retail Investment Strategy contains no ban on inducements, and the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (FSA) has paused its domestic study of them. Occupational pension capital grew 18%, against 7% for the market. The Riksbank held its policy rate at 1.75% through Q2 and Q3; Barclays, Deutsche Bank, Nordea and the forward curve all expect a hike to 2.0% on 4 November, the first upward move since 2023.

Evidence: the headwinds are cyclical and fast. Transactions fell 8% quarter on quarter in Q3 and 10% year on year in September (Nordnet's fell 5%, flatexDEGIRO's 3%). The macro regime is risk-off: the US ten-year yield is near 5.1%, and Viewforth has cut Sweden's country tilt to Neutral because a hike lands on fast-resetting mortgages. The krona is strong, which matters because foreign trading is 31% of turnover and 70% of that is in US shares. The post-election tax debate has made a bank tax, a redesign of the ISK and the deductibility of endowment insurance live questions.

Inference. The external forces are better than eighteen months ago on the two issues that de-rated the stock (rates and the threatened inducement ban) and on the structural asset leg. They are worse on the activity leg and on yield per unit, where Nordnet, SAVR, Montrose and the shift to passive funds each take a little.

So what. The external picture supports the model's volume lines (savings capital +10% to 12% a year) with high confidence. The one dated external positive inside six months is the Riksbank decision; the one external negative to watch is a reversal in US retail trading or in the AI trade, which would hit brokerage and currency income together.

Counter-case. The bear case says the structural leg is also slowing: DNB Carnegie puts controllable net-inflow growth at about 6% of opening capital, below the 10% that Avanza's 2030 target needs, and most of the 21% capital growth comes from rising markets. The point is true, and our base already uses 6%.

Where I differ from the market. The sell-side over-weights the rate lever (every bull note leads with "4% EPS on the forward curve") and under-weights the deposit-beta history that caps the lever on the way up. The sell-side also under-weights the effect of the risk-off regime on trading velocity over the next two quarters. I agree with the market that regulation is now net supportive.

What would change my view. A Riksbank hold in November; trades per customer falling a further 10% in Q4; a signal from the Ministry of Finance that a profit-based bank tax is coming before 2028.

Score: 55. Structural tailwinds in the top third of European companies, offset by a live cyclical downturn in trading activity and a risk-off regime that acts on 44% of revenue.

#2. Internally driven corporate change forces

The pointAvanza's internal forces are a stabiliser, not an accelerant: the one internal change that moved earnings (the deposit internalisation) is complete, and the next ones are 2028 to 2030 events worth low single digits of EPS each.

Evidence: the team is rebuilt. Gustaf Unger (CEO since March 2024) has rebuilt the executive team, which now has eleven members: a new CFO (January 2026, after 21 years at SEB), a new COO (March), a new CEO of Avanza Fonder (May) and a Denmark country manager (October, from Lunar and Saxo). The board is unchanged, and the founding shareholders (the Hagströmer family with 10.1% and Creades with 10.1%) are aligned and passive.

Evidence: Strategy 2030 has moved from articulation to execution on all five priorities, as the table below shows. Two details matter beyond the table. In occupational pensions, Avanza is petitioning to remove the employer signature that currently blocks a quarter of pension transfers. In Private Banking, Avanza has added mortgage tiers above SEK 30m.

Evidence: the largest internal change of the period is done. When the FSA forced the closure of the Sparkonto+ product, Avanza internalised SEK 25bn of its deposits at ten times the spread it had earned on them. That internalisation is complete and in the run rate: Avanza's own savings accounts doubled to SEK 66bn, and Q2 net interest income (NII) reached SEK 486m.

Evidence: the negatives. Headcount rose 15% to 812 and costs rose 12% year on year in Q3. Efficiency gains are being reinvested rather than banked (management says it has "more initiatives than capacity"). New mortgages for customers with SEK 3m to 10m were paused because the leverage ratio bound. There is no buyback despite a renewed 10% authorisation. And management frames as "temporary" a yield decline that its own strategy causes.

Inference. The next internal changes (Denmark, Sigma, pensions and the cost cap stepping down to 5% in 2030) each add low single digits of EPS, and none lands before 2028. What the internal picture does deliver is predictability: of the cost line (four straight years under guide) and of the recurring revenue base.

So what. Model costs at the guide less 1%, Denmark as a cost line to 2030, and Sigma and pensions as options. Expect no margin expansion before 2030 and no step-up in capital returns before 2028. The internal risk is not that any one initiative fails; it is that a larger fixed cost base meets a drifting revenue margin, which Q3 showed for the first time.

Counter-case. The bull case says the rebuilt team is exactly what the next phase needs, and that Denmark's under-budget build and the cloud migration's on-time milestones show a builder's capability emerging. That is possible, and the first six months of evidence are favourable. But the real test, a second platform in a second country against a 20-year incumbent, does not report before mid-2028.

Where I differ from the market. The market reads Avanza's management as cautious and Nordnet's as ambitious, and prices the two accordingly. I think the market is right on growth and wrong on quality. Three marks show the better-run company: Avanza expenses its development while Nordnet capitalises SEK 178m of personnel cost a year; Avanza's Additional Tier 1 (AT1) capital costs STIBOR plus 2.85% against Nordnet's plus 5.0%; and Avanza has met its cost cap every year. Those marks will matter more in a downturn than in a boom. I agree with the market that there is no near-term upgrade impulse from inside the company.

What would change my view. Positive: a 2027 Swedish cost guide at or below 7% with the Danish budget held, or a first statement that AI or cloud productivity is being banked (which would be unprecedented). Negative: a rise in the Danish budget or a launch slipping into 2028.

Score: 52. A complete, disciplined team executing bounded adjacencies inside a published cost envelope, with the one earnings-moving change already in the base and no pricing or capital-allocation lever in use.

#3. Value chain, business model, financial profile, management

The pointAvanza's structure protects what it has (customers, capital and its cost ratio) extremely well, but protects less well what it needs to grow (yield per unit, relative growth and the multiple); the structural gap is pricing power, which Avanza's promise to customers rules out by design.

Evidence: a favourable duopoly. The digital investing tier in Sweden is a duopoly at fee parity, in which Avanza holds twice Nordnet's share of Swedish savings and both operators earn margins above 70%. Neither uses list price as a weapon: both held prices through the 2022 to 2023 trough, and Nordnet says that matching Swedish prices in Denmark would cost it 1% of income. Banks keep losing flows despite their stated digital ambitions. Entrants (eToro, Levler, Scalable) have taken no share in five years against the barriers of BankID, ISK tax reporting and brand trust. Substitutes also run toward the platforms, whose share of inflows exceeds their share of the stock of savings.

Evidence: an owned route to market and a moat that passes every test. Avanza acquires customers directly, at about SEK 590 each, against a lifetime value many times that. Beyond the moat measures in the tiles below, Avanza serves 450,000 to 490,000 daily active users on one Java technology stack that deploys in minutes, runs 23 own funds holding 41% of fund capital, and holds three regulated licences.

Evidence: the best financial profile in the peer set, like for like. Avanza's Q3 return on equity of 44% compares with Nordnet's 38% to 42% (flattered by capitalised development), Fineco's 25% and AJ Bell's 33% (flattered by interest on cash). Reported and adjusted EPS differ by 0.2%. Capital expenditure was SEK 74m against net income of SEK 2,609m.

Evidence: management is a disciplined administrator, not yet a builder. Executives receive fixed cash pay only and bought their warrants at market prices. Avanza publishes the best monthly disclosure in the sector, has set stretching 2030 targets (SEK 2,000bn of savings capital, a 35% return on equity and 8% average cost growth) and runs a culture congruent with its model. Management is not a yield manager: it says itself that its brokerage pricing may not align with its simplicity goals.

Inference. Two forces erode what Avanza needs to grow. The second duopolist, Nordnet, compounds on a four-market platform. And the fee pool per unit of savings drifts down through mix, niche pricing at the affluent end and regulation.

So what. Carry the volume lines, churn and costs with high confidence for four years. Carry the revenue margin as the one line that Avanza's advantage does not protect. Do not expect management to lift revenue per unit or to add a buyback before 2028. For the multiple: in the post-2022 regime, quality of this order has earned 20x to 21x when the stock was delivering, and that range is the ceiling toward which the fair-multiple judgement works.

Counter-case. Nordnet now out-grows Avanza on every measure, is broadening into Avanza's affluent target market through a private-banking venture with ABG Sundal Collier, and launches in Germany in November. If market share consolidates toward the largest platform rather than the lowest-cost one, Avanza's home advantage does not travel. The evidence says that consolidation at home still favours the lowest-cost, highest-satisfaction operator (Avanza's share rises half a point a year), but the regional pull favours Nordnet.

Where I differ from the market. The market values Nordnet 3 turns of earnings above Avanza for its growth and footprint. I would pay more than the market does for Avanza's economics and less for Nordnet's growth. I expect the valuation spread to narrow over two years as Nordnet's German costs and Avanza's Danish disclosures arrive together, but I agree that the spread is correctly signed today.

What would change my view. Evidence of Private Banking or Pro customers' assets migrating to Montrose or SAVR (no such evidence exists today, and the data gap is real); a list-price cut to the 25 basis point standard currency fee (worth SEK 100m to 150m a year); a documented outage under load that moves customers.

Score: 78. A top-decile franchise, financial profile and culture in a favourable duopoly, marked down for the absence of pricing power, the regional scale gap and an administrator rather than a builder at the top.

#4. Guidance conservatism, expectation management and the delivery record

The pointManagement beats the 30% of the income statement it guides (costs) and offers no guidance or cushion on the 70% it does not (revenue), so guidance can supply an upgrade worth under 1% of profit and nothing more.

Evidence: what Avanza guides. Avanza guides on costs, capital and its 2030 targets only. The cost guide is Swedish cost growth of 9% in 2026 (reiterated four quarters running) plus SEK 40m for Denmark, then 8% on average to 2030 and about 5% in 2030. Avanza also publishes a rate sensitivity each quarter, a phased Danish budget with its capitalisation split, and a self-compiled consensus (18 contributors for Q3).

Evidence: the cost record. Avanza beat its cost guide in each of the last four years (table below). Nine-month 2026 costs of SEK 1,145m imply a Q4 of about SEK 430m and a full year of SEK 1,575m, against the SEK 1,580m guide.

Evidence: the earnings record. On earnings Avanza gives no guidance and no cushion. Results have beaten consensus by 4% to 5% in quarters of rising volatility (Q2 2026: +4%) and missed by 2% to 5% in quiet ones (Q3 2026 and Q2 2025: -2% each). The one large miss came in 2022, when EPS fell 19% after the sell-side had extrapolated 2021. Avanza missed its 15% savings-capital growth target in 2025 (13%) and meets it in 2026 only with help from markets.

Evidence: the tone after Q3. Management's commentary ("another strong quarter"; yield compression is "temporary"; "a gradual economic turnaround") is more confident than the run rate. The 2027 revenue consensus needs both a recovery in trading velocity and the rate path in the forward curve.

Inference. The guidance that exists is set to be beaten modestly, and it will be. The guidance the market would need (revenue, margin and EPS) does not exist, so the sell-side anchors its revenue line to markets, the Riksbank and management's tone, and the tone after Q3 leans high. Management is an honest tracker, not a serial sandbagger.

So what. The only guidance event with signalling power in the horizon is the 2027 Swedish cost guide on 22 January. My central case is a guide of 7% to 8% (45% probability, with 25% on a guide at or below 7%), which would be the first visible step down of the cost framework and would land at our base. Even so, the group cost total including Denmark (+13%) sits above consensus costs (about SEK 1,748m implied, against our SEK 1,780m), so brokers who carry Denmark light will trim 2027 EBIT by 1% to 2% on a day when the headline reads well.

Counter-case. A company that never guides on earnings cannot disappoint on guidance, and Avanza's cost discipline through a rate cycle from 4.0% down to 1.75% is a record few financials match. Agreed; the point is that this record does not generate the upgrade mechanics that Richard's framework looks for.

Where I differ from the market. The market treats the cost beat as proof of conservatism across the business. I treat it as proof of conservatism on the 30% of the income statement the company controls, and as proof of nothing about the 70% it does not. The dividend proposal is a small negative the market has not noticed: our dividend per share of SEK 14.3 is below consensus at SEK 14.52, and a payout above 76% would be a surprise.

What would change my view. Negative: a 2027 Swedish cost guide above 8.5%. Positive: a payout above 78%, a first buyback, or any quantified efficiency promise.

Score: 48. Exemplary conservatism and delivery on the one line Avanza guides, no earnings guidance at all, a soft-quarter framing that runs ahead of the numbers, and no history of raising anything.

#5. The profit-conversion mechanics: pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost scope, feedback loops

The pointAvanza's high operating leverage sets the size of the forecast error but will not drive earnings before 2030: costs are 90% fixed and pre-committed, unit pricing drifts down by design, and every loop that compounds volume is matched by one that caps yield.

Evidence: operating leverage. The cost base (SEK 1,413m in 2025; about SEK 1,780m in 2027 including Denmark) is 90% fixed within a year: personnel 60%, IT 15%, external services 7% and depreciation 7%. Only transaction costs and payment commissions flex. A 10% change in revenue therefore moves operating profit by about 15%. In 2022 income fell 10% and profit fell 21%, as costs rose 19%; in 2025 income rose 15% and profit 17%.

Evidence: pricing power is negative. Unit prices drift down by 1.0 to 1.5 points of revenue growth a year through mix: the affluent share of trading, the index-fund share of fund capital and the 12.5 basis point manual currency account. Management has never cut costs in a downturn; its response in 2022 was to hold cost growth. The one positive price lever is deposit pricing: Avanza passed through 75% to 80% of rate cuts in 2024 to 2025 but only 36% of the 2022 to 2023 hikes (its cumulative deposit beta), which is why its net interest income sensitivity is asymmetric.

Evidence: financial leverage is nil, and the capital constraint is loosening. Avanza's only financing is SEK 1.3bn of perpetual AT1 capital and small leases; the SEK 119bn of "debt" that FactSet shows is customer deposits. The binding constraint is the regulatory leverage ratio (4.8% against a 3.5% requirement), and it is loosening by 15 to 30 basis points a year. If ever needed, Avanza could cut 10% to 15% of its cost base within a year (deferring Denmark, cutting external services, freezing hiring), but it has never used that lever.

Evidence: the feedback loops sort cleanly. Every reinforcing loop acts on volume; every balancing loop acts on yield or capital, including the moat's own engine of sharing scale with customers.

Inference: in the base case, revenue growth produces slightly smaller profit growth until 2030. Revenue grows 8% and operating profit 6% in 2027; profit grows 8% to 9% in 2028 to 2029 and 9% in 2030, when the Swedish cost growth rate reaches 5% and the Danish marketing cap lapses. The reason is that Avanza's cost escalator is fixed in advance and the Danish expansion bill sits on top of it.

Inference: the operating leverage is symmetrical in arithmetic and asymmetrical in practice. The arithmetic multiplier is 1.45x in both directions. In practice, a revenue shortfall passes through in full because management does not cut costs, and a revenue beat passes through in full because the costs are already spent. The incremental margin on each year's revenue change is 76% in 2026, 53% in 2027 and 70% to 82% thereafter, so it dilutes the 68% average margin only in 2027.

So what. For the next three years the operating leverage sets the error bars rather than driving earnings. It becomes a driver again from 2030: a 72% to 75% margin is reachable on 8% revenue growth once cost growth is down to 4% to 5%, which is outside the horizon but inside a three-year narrative. Within the horizon, the profit-conversion case depends on two things rather than on cost. The first is the deposit loop at a 2% policy rate: a dash to cash adds net interest income while brokerage falls, a stabiliser that did not exist at a 0% rate in 2022. The second is the trading-velocity line.

Counter-case. DNB Carnegie values a return of H1 2026 trading velocity at 17% of 2027 EPS: that is the operating leverage working upward, and it needs no management action. Correct, and it is the bull case. The 2022 to 2023 precedent, two years of lower activity after a peak, is why I carry it as a 25%-probability case rather than the base.

Where I differ from the market. Consensus's 69.5% operating margin for 2027 implicitly assumes that the operating leverage works for earnings in 2027; our 68.2% says that it works against them. On pricing power the market and I agree: there is none, by design.

What would change my view. A Swedish cost guide that steps down faster than the framework; the first visible banking of AI or cloud productivity; a list-price response to SAVR or Montrose, which would be the one step-change in the pricing picture.

Score: 45. High fixed-cost operating leverage that will not help earnings before 2030, negative unit pricing by design, no financial leverage, a cost-out lever the company has never pulled, and feedback loops that compound volume and cap yield in equal measure.

#6. Forecast financials and the scope for faster growth or higher margins than the past

The pointOur base is a 9% EPS compounder with a 4% dividend yield and no margin expansion before 2030; it runs 3% to 5% below consensus from FY2027 onward, and the real gap with consensus is the 2027 operating margin.

The base case, which the model reproduces (SEK m, company basis):

Net interest income and fund commissions do most of the growth to 2030; brokerage and currency, the trading-velocity lines, grow least. The chart and table below give each revenue line's path and the assumptions behind it.

The EPS definition explains part of the gap with consensus, and the 2027 margin explains the rest. Our EPS deducts the AT1 coupon (about SEK 0.38 a share), as DNB Carnegie's does; FactSet does not say whether its median does. On a pre-coupon basis our FY2027 EPS is SEK 20.6, only 1.3% below consensus. The real gap is therefore the 2027 operating margin.

Scope for double-digit growth: not in the base. The FY2025 to FY2030 EPS compound growth rate is 8.8%, with 2027 at 6% as the trough and 9% by 2030. Double-digit growth needs one of three things the base does not carry: a return of H1 2026 trading velocity (worth 7.5 points of growth in the year it returns), a second rate hike (2.7 points), or Swedish cost growth reaching 5% earlier than 2030. The 2027 upside case (EPS of SEK 22.5, +11%) is double-digit growth for one year, not a new trend.

Scope for higher growth or margins than the past: no on both over four years. Revenue growth roughly halves, from 15% a year in 2023 to 2026 to 7.5% to 8.5%, because the three tailwinds that made those years exceptional are already in the base and cannot repeat: the 2022 to 2023 rate cycle, which took net interest income from SEK 321m to SEK 1.6bn; the deposit internalisation; and the H1 2026 trading peak. The operating margin plateaus at 68% to 69.5% because two effects cancel: the scale benefit on costs (cost to capital falls from 13.9 to 11.7 basis points) and the yield drift on revenue. Return on equity drifts from 42% to 38% as equity compounds faster than earnings at a 75% payout. The regime change is in Avanza's growth, not in its robustness.

Quarterly shape for the next 18 months: Q1 2027 is the likeliest beat, Q2 2027 the likeliest miss, and Q4 2027 carries the horizon's lowest margin. For Q4 2026 we expect income of about SEK 1,290m (consensus needs about SEK 1,350m), costs of about SEK 430m (the seasonal peak), operating profit of about SEK 860m and EPS of about SEK 4.55, against an implied consensus of about SEK 4.80. Q1 2027 benefits from a full quarter of the hike and an easy cost comparison. Q2 2027 is compared with the Q2 2026 income peak of SEK 1,334m. Q4 2027 stacks Danish launch costs on the seasonal cost peak, for a 66.3% margin. The chart gives each quarter's income and operating profit; quarterly EPS for 2027 runs at about SEK 5.1, 5.0, 5.1 and 5.0.

Where I differ from the market. Consensus is right in direction (a deceleration to high single-digit growth) and too high in two places: the revenue margin, where consensus implies 43 to 43.5 basis points for 2027, and the phasing of Danish costs, which consensus carries SEK 30m to 80m light. Deutsche Bank's 14% EPS compound growth rate to 2028 is the top of the range, not the middle; DNB Carnegie's 8% is already below ours.

What would change my view. Upward: October to December statistics showing trades per customer back above the Q2 2026 level; Q4 brokerage income above SEK 330m; income per customer above SEK 2,300. Downward: a Q1 2027 brokerage yield below 10 basis points; deposits below 8.5% of savings capital with no hike; income per customer below SEK 2,050.

Score: 42. A 9% EPS compounder with a 4% yield and no margin expansion before 2030, growing more slowly than its own past and more slowly than consensus allows for 2027 to 2028.

#7. Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and narrative over 6 to 12 months

The pointThe estimate cycle has peaked: a cut to FY2027 consensus is six times as likely as a raise, the cuts land in the next two revision rounds, and an investor who wants the upgrade phase should want to own the shares from late January, not from today.

Evidence: estimates have stalled at their high. FY2027 consensus EPS is up 13% over twelve months, 8% over six, 2% over three and 1% over one. The FactSet mean (SEK 21.14 on 9 October, SEK 21.12 on 22 October) did not move through a 2% operating profit miss in which every revenue line came in below consensus. Ten of the thirteen houses are still on numbers from before the Q3 report, two of them from July. The share of Buy ratings is 50%, and the mean target price is SEK 416.

Evidence: the three notes published since the Q3 report split three ways. DNB Carnegie trimmed (FY2026 EPS SEK 18.90, FY2028 SEK 20.79, target SEK 425); Deutsche Bank held (FY2027 SEK 22.85, target SEK 440); Jefferies held its Underperform rating (target SEK 335). Guidance cannot be raised in any sense the market rewards (#4).

Evidence: the research narrative has absorbed the words of the Q3 decoupling but not its arithmetic. No house writes the 2027 margin as the line that will disappoint, none models the quarterly shape, and none mentions the loosening of the leverage ratio or the irrelevance of the risk tax.

Inference: my probabilities for FY2027 consensus EPS over the next 18 months. A cut of more than 2% has a 60% probability; no change, 30%; a raise of more than 2%, 10%. The central outcome is SEK 20.0 to 20.5 by April 2028, with the cuts concentrated in the Q4 consensus compilation and the 22 January report. FY2028 consensus falls 3% to 6% as analysts model the Danish running cost and a second year of yield drift.

Inference: a net rise in consensus inside twelve months has only about a 10% probability. It needs either a return of H1 2026 trading velocity (20% to 25% probability) or two of the following to coincide before Denmark is modelled: a second hike (40%), deposits rebuilding (35%) and a Swedish cost guide below 7% (25%).

So what. The scope for upgrades in the next six months is low, but the scope for a turn in the narrative in months six to twelve is real. Three events open it: the Q1 report on 16 April 2027, the first likely beat; the first Danish disclosures in H1 2027, the first new information on the export story; and the April annual general meeting, where the buyback question is first asked. The sequence is cuts, then stabilisation, then the first upgrade candidates.

Counter-case. Deutsche Bank argues that the asset engine overwhelms the yield drift within 2027, so consensus is too low rather than too high. A strong Q4 for inflows (a risk-off quarter drives flows to funds and savings accounts) plus a rate hike could make the January report a non-event and let the spring upgrades arrive without a preceding cut. If Q4 brokerage income holds near SEK 310m and net interest income reaches SEK 480m, the miss against an already-trimmed consensus would be 2% to 3% rather than 5%, and the shares might not need to re-test SEK 330.

Where I differ from the market. The dashboard's sell-side momentum rating of A reflects a twelve-month lookback; I would mark it B now and expect C by the spring. I agree with DNB Carnegie's frame ("growth must come from assets; yields will not return to peak") and differ from its estimate only in carrying slightly less yield drift.

What would change my view. A Riksbank hold in November, which would deepen the next revision round from -3% to -6%; a second hike in February, which would hold FY2027 consensus and lift net interest income estimates by 3% to 4%; a January consensus compilation showing the lagging brokers already down 3%, in which case the cut is in the price before the report.

Score: 35. Estimates at a twelve-month high after a miss, with a 60% probability of a 2% to 4% cut in the next two rounds and a 10% probability of a net raise inside a year; the upgrade window opens in the spring, not now.

#8. Current momentum: guidance, estimates, narrative, technicals, and the same for peers

The pointThere is no momentum to buy today: momentum is negative on every reading that leads and positive only on the twelve-month estimate breadth, which lags; the shares have also stopped amplifying the sector and now trade on their own news.

Evidence: guidance, estimates and narrative. Guidance momentum is flat: apart from one favourable SEK 10m change to the Danish budget, nothing has moved in four quarters. Estimate momentum is positive on the twelve-month lookback (the dashboard's A, with a revision score of 10), stalled over one month (+1%) and negative in the three notes written since the Q3 report. The research narrative is a rate-and-volume story ("17% upside if H1 activity returns"; the Riksbank is "the most powerful near-term catalyst"), while a quarter of the houses, led by Jefferies (a restricted Sell at SEK 360), argue a structural decline of income per customer. The files contain no observation of retail or domestic institutional commentary, which is a gap.

Evidence: technicals. The technical momentum rating is D.

Evidence: peers. Nordnet is the sector's momentum stock: technical rating B, sell-side rating A, +22% over twelve months and at the 44th percentile of its multiple range; the market absorbed its 2% Q3 miss on 22 October, and DNB Carnegie cut its Nordnet target to SEK 380 "on lower peer multiples". Fineco is rated A by the sell-side but D on technicals. Deutsche Bank downgraded flatexDEGIRO in October (technical F, revision score 0). The leveraged brokers (IG, Plus500 and Swissquote) are in retreat on both revisions and price. Every asset-gathering platform except Nordnet sits in the bottom quarter of its own multiple range.

Inference. Momentum is negative on the readings that lead (technicals, revisions since the Q3 report and the tone of the narrative) and positive only on the reading that lags (twelve-month revision breadth). Because the shares now trade on their own news rather than amplifying the sector, the effect cuts both ways: delivery can re-rate the shares without help from the sector, and a sector recovery would lift them at a beta of only 0.7 to 1.

So what. There is no momentum to buy today and no sector re-rating in progress to lean on. The price now sits at the 200-day average with a D rating, which is exactly the "bullish below SEK 360" level set in the first analysis set; but the price reached that level on momentum, not on fundamentals.

Counter-case. The 200-day average has risen for ten of the last twelve months, and the shares are up 10% over nine months. A stock that holds its 200-day average through a 7% sector drawdown and a 2% earnings miss is showing relative strength under the surface, and a rate hike on 4 November is a scheduled catalyst inside two weeks. The point is fair, and it is why I would not short the shares at the trough band.

Where I differ from the market. The sell-side still ranks Avanza as its second-favourite platform after Nordnet (50% Buy ratings; median target SEK 430, 19% above the price), but the price action says the buyers have already left. I side with the price for the next two reports and with the sell-side's targets after that.

What would change my view. A close above the 50-day average (about SEK 388) on the Riksbank decision. Nordnet's German launch data in January: a strong start widens the growth gap with Avanza and a weak one narrows it. The 0.74 correlation makes Nordnet the most useful read-across and the most useful hedge.

Score: 35. Guidance flat, estimates peaking, narrative softening and technicals at D on the 200-day average, with the one peer the market pays for growth still rising and the rest of the cohort in retreat.

#9. Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

The pointThe Avanza case is simple to structure and track, but not precisely forecastable: two inputs the company does not control explain three-quarters of the forecast error, and the FY2027 range of outcomes leans down into the next two reports.

Simplicity: the case is among the simplest in European financials to structure and monitor. Avanza has four revenue lines on one base (savings capital multiplied by a margin for each line), one guided cost number, nothing below the operating line that surprises, one segment and, until H2 2027, one country. It discloses every volume driver monthly, in the first week of each month.

Five drivers explain the whole difference between the next four years and the last four: the absence of a rate and activity tailwind, the yield drift, the Danish bill, the cost escalator stepping down, and the drag below the operating line. Two inputs the company does not control explain 75% to 80% of the variance around the forecast: trading velocity, set by realised market volatility, and the policy rate, acting through deposits. That concentration makes the case trackable but not precisely forecastable.

Fragilities and requirements.

  • Operating leverage on volatile revenue. 44% of revenue is transactional and 90% of the cost base is fixed, so each 10% of revenue is 15% of EPS, and 10% swings in revenue are ordinary. Management does not cut costs in a down year.
  • The yield drift is the one judgement that leans on reasoning rather than precedent. The base assumes a slower drift (1.2 basis points a year) than the recent record (2 to 3).
  • The base asks for growth Avanza has not delivered without a cycle behind it. Avanza has never grown earnings 6% to 9% a year without a rate or activity cycle: 2016 to 2019, the only cycle-free period, was flat to down. Hargreaves Lansdown in 2012 to 2017 and Avanza itself in 2023 to 2025 show, however, that asset compounding can carry revenue through heavier yield erosion than the base asks for.

The FY2027 range of outcomes leans down: the probability-weighted EPS of about SEK 19.9 sits 5% below consensus. FY2027 EPS ranges from SEK 16 to 23 around a base of SEK 20.2. One standard deviation is about plus or minus 10%; the bull tail (+11%) and the bear tail (-20%) each carry roughly 25% probability. The bear case does not need a recession, only eighteen months of low volatility after a peak, which 2022 to 2023 delivered without one. By the Q1 2028 report the range for FY2028 EPS widens to SEK 17 to 25. The matching range for the share price, on FY2029 forward earnings, runs from about SEK 300 (bear EPS at 15.9x) to SEK 560 (bull EPS at 21x).

Suddenness, predictability and trackability: the error concentrates exactly where disclosure is thinnest. Trading velocity moves in weeks and is visible monthly, and even daily through broker web-traffic trackers that explain about half of each month's change. The rate path moves on dated decisions (4 November, February and April). The yield mix moves slowly and is visible only quarterly, with a lag, which is why Q3's 5% brokerage miss came on volumes the monthly data had already shown. Avanza's two disclosure gaps sit on the lines where the error concentrates: there is no intra-quarter disclosure of fee-class or segment mix, and no disclosure of realised deposit pass-through. Read-across shocks are the ordinary condition of the sector (flatexDEGIRO's downgrade; IG -45% in three months) and hit Avanza at a beta of about 0.7.

Materiality to the share price: on the multiple alone the downside is small, and it takes an earnings cut to reach double digits. With a 10% earnings cut the fair trough is SEK 310 to 345; with the full bear case it is about SEK 300. The exit trigger set earlier, a sequential operating margin below 50%, is far away (Q3 was 72%).

Sector and cyclical precedents. In 2022 EPS fell 19% and the two-year-forward multiple fell from 32x to 14x within twelve months, after a boom the sell-side had extrapolated. In Q1 2023 a 4% miss on deposit remuneration was followed by twelve months of multiple compression to 15x before net interest income rescued the year.

The sector's recurring false friend is rate dependence: AJ Bell, Fineco, Nordnet and Avanza all de-rated as rates fell. Its recurring re-rating comes from a visible shift toward asset-scaled fees. Avanza has the lowest share of net interest income of the four (33%) and the clearest shift toward asset fees, and it has just shown a mild case of the sector's other false friend, lazy extrapolation of a cyclical peak. Fineco's exit from the UK in 2023, after six years, is the honest base rate for greenfield platform entries, which is why Denmark is carried as a cost only.

Where I differ from the market. The dashboard's Case Riskiness rating of B (as at 22 September) pre-dates the Q3 report and the turn in activity; I share the third analysis set's view that the case is "neither the simple low-risk setup B suggests nor a fragile one". Against the sell-side, I weight one risk more: the downward lean of the range of outcomes into the next two reports. I weight two risks less: Denmark (bounded at 2% to 3% of EPS a year plus a possible overrun of 1% to 2%) and the risk tax (removed from the four-year forecast range).

What would change my view. A documented outage under load with visible outflows, which is the one operational risk with no disclosed data; a Danish fee schedule that undercuts Nordnet's 25 basis point currency fee, which could start a Danish price war worth up to SEK 200m across both platforms; the FSA re-opening a domestic study of inducements (fund commissions are 17% of income, 60% of them Swedish).

Score: 55. Simple to structure, trackable monthly, with no solvency or franchise risk, but with 1.45x operating leverage on a 44% transactional revenue base, a one-standard-deviation EPS range of plus or minus 10%, a downside lean into the next two reports, and a sector history of 20% earnings falls when activity peaks pass.

#10. Where the stock is in its lifecycle

The pointThe stock is in three phases at once (stalling on earnings, bottoming on price, reinforcing on assets), which is the characteristic shape of a quality stock three to six months before its revision trough, so the right posture is patience on entry and a plan to add on the dated events that would mark the turn.

Evidence.

  • Earnings momentum is decelerating: operating income growth of +26% (Q2), +12% (Q3), about +3% (Q4 base) and +6% for 2027; quarterly EPS of SEK 4.71, 4.97, 4.90 and about 4.55.
  • Estimate momentum has peaked, with cuts ahead (#7).
  • Price and multiple are at the low end: 12% below the 52-week high, 17% above the 52-week low, at the 200-day average, at the 12th percentile of ten years and the 5th of two.
  • The asset engine is at its strongest since 2021: savings capital +21%, net inflows +61%, a 32% share of Swedish fund flows.
  • Scope for upgrades is low for six months and real from the spring.
  • Risk factors have rotated from the rate-cut axis (now dissolved) to the risk-off axis (trading velocity, deposits and markets) and to monetisation per unit.

Inference. In Richard's taxonomy the stock is stalling on the earnings and estimate readings: growth is decelerating, Avanza has posted its first miss, estimates sit at a twelve-month high and the technical rating is D. The price and multiple are bottoming: the shares sit at a fair trough band, no longer amplify the sector, and the idiosyncratic share of their variance has risen to about two-thirds. The asset engine beneath both is reinforcing.

The stock is not collapsing (margin 72%, return on equity 44%, churn 0.7%), and it is not yet turning up. A turn needs three things: income per customer stabilising above SEK 2,100, a Q1 2027 beat in the first quarter with a full hike, and the first Danish disclosures. Viewforth's Phases page calls the phase "Turning/Inflecting", which is right about the price and early about the earnings.

So what. The phase argues for patience on entry and for a fair multiple in the lower half of the range (#11). It also argues for a plan to add on the dated events that would mark the turn: when a stock moves from stalling to turning up with a reinforcing asset engine beneath it, the fundamental skew and the upgrade skew align, and that alignment is six months away, not two years.

Counter-case. A bear would say this is the start of a two-year stalling phase like 2022 to 2023, and that the asset engine's strength merely reflects a market at its highs. The difference from 2022 is a 2% policy rate, which lets the deposit loop cushion a risk-off year, and a 12th-percentile multiple rather than 32x. The shape is the same; the amplitude is about a third.

Where I differ from the market. The sell-side (50% Buy ratings; targets 19% above the price) still has the stock in a delivering phase, and the price has it bottoming. I have it stalling, with a dated turn ahead.

What would change my view. Income per customer below SEK 2,050 in Q4, which would extend the stalling phase and make the bear case live; or above SEK 2,300 in Q1 2027, which would make the turn early and the bull case live.

Score: 45. Stalling on earnings and estimates, bottoming on price and multiple, reinforcing on assets: a less favourable phase than a turning or broadening stock, and a more favourable one than a stock whose foundations are in doubt.

#11. The fair multiple

The pointMy fair multiple is 19.5x two-year-forward earnings for the next 6 to 18 months, rising to 21x by 2029 if the turn is evidenced; Viewforth's 22.15x guideline is a delivering-phase multiple and the ceiling of the post-2022 regime.

The guideline and its history. Viewforth's rule maps the stock's phase onto its own ten-year range of the two-year-forward P/E (10th percentile 15.9x, 35th 19.3x, median 21.0x, 60th 22.15x, 75th 24.3x, 90th 27.7x, with one outlier month excluded). The Phases page (23 October) assigns the "Turning/Inflecting" phase and a guideline of 22.15x, 28% above the current 17.25x. The model's one-page summary was computed on an earlier guideline of 27.70x, the 90th-percentile "mania" band. The third analysis set rightly flagged that figure as the largest inconsistency in the files; it has since been superseded, so this memo works from 22.15x as the guideline.

My view: 19.5x for the next 6 to 18 months, and 21x by 2029 if the staircase of evidence delivers. Three reasons support it.

  1. The phase calls for the lower half of the range. Viewforth's rule puts stalling or turning-up stocks lower in the range, because their forecasts are more uncertain, and peak-delivery stocks higher. #10 puts Avanza in a stalling phase on earnings with a dated turn ahead. 22.15x is a delivering-phase multiple for this stock: the stock last sustained it in 2025, a year of 15% EPS growth with rates falling and retail investors re-risking. The 60th percentile is the right destination once the turn is evidenced (a Q1 2027 beat, income per customer above SEK 2,100 and Denmark on budget), which makes 22.15x a 2028 multiple, not a 2027 one.
  2. The ten-year range is inflated by a regime that will not recur. The ten-year history includes the 2020 to 2021 boom (30x to 44x) and the 2022 collapse. Since mid-2022 the monthly two-year-forward multiple has run from 13.8x to 22.4x, with a median near 18x and a 75th percentile near 20x. On that regime's own distribution, 19.5x is about the 70th percentile and 22.15x is the top. The stock reached 22x only once (January 2025) and held 20x to 21x through 2025 while delivering mid-teens growth. Deutsche Bank observes that the stock trades at a 30% discount to its ten-year average and that historical averages may no longer anchor it; that is right for the average and wrong for the floor, which has held at 15.9x to 16.5x through three bad windows.
  3. The cross-section of peers brackets 19.5x. Nordnet, at 19.3x to 19.5x, is the ceiling within 18 months: Avanza would need to close the growth and export gap to pass it. The sector median of 15.2x is the floor; AJ Bell (15.2x), Fineco (15.3x) and Integrafin (14.2x) bracket the cohort. A 19.5x multiple puts Avanza a turn below the peer the market pays for growth and four turns above the cohort median. That is where a company with a 40% return on equity, a clean income statement, 9% EPS compounding and a 4% yield belongs while its narrative has no new chapter until H2 2027.

What the fair multiple is worth. On FY2029 EPS of SEK 23.3 (the two-year-forward earnings at end-2027), 19.5x gives SEK 454 (+26% on the price), 22.15x gives SEK 516 (+43%), and the current multiple held gives SEK 402 (+12%). The 2.65-turn difference between my view and the guideline is 17% of the price, the biggest single judgement in the memo (#0).

Counter-case. If the yield compression proves cyclical and Q1 2027 confirms it, the market will not wait for Denmark to re-rate the shares. 2025 shows that the stock earns 20x to 21x in a delivering year within a quarter of the evidence arriving, and the guideline's 22.15x would then be reached by mid-2027 rather than 2028. I give this about a one-in-three probability, which is why 19.5x is a central estimate with a right tail.

Where I differ from the market. The sell-side's median target of SEK 430 is 18.5x FY2029 earnings or 20.6x FY2027 earnings: the bulls already pay 20x to 21x on 2027 estimates that are 3% too high. At the 18-month horizon I am below the sell-side on earnings and close to it on the multiple; the difference between us is timing.

What would change my view. Up to 21x: income per customer above SEK 2,300, or a Danish fee schedule and account wrapper that undercut Nordnet without a margin collapse. Down to 17x: a Riksbank hold in November, a Q1 2027 brokerage yield below 10 basis points, or a Swedish bank tax on profit.

Score: 60. A fair multiple of 19.5x against 17.25x now gives 13% of re-rating scope in the base and 28% to the guideline in the delivering case, with a floor that has held at 16x: more scope than most European financials at the bottom of their ranges, and less than the guideline implies.

#12. Total shareholder return, decomposed

The pointEarnings and dividends give a dependable 13% a year; the multiple decides everything above that, and the probability-weighted return to end-2027 is about +25%, with a one-in-four chance of a double-digit loss and a three-in-four chance of a gain above 30%.

How the model summary's +77.5% arises, and why it should not be read as given. The one-page summary shows +77.5% to 31 December 2027 (62% annualised) and +103.7% to 30 June 2029, at the superseded 27.70x guideline and a price of SEK 380.2 (13 October). The arithmetic runs as follows. Two-year-forward EPS in the 18-month column is FY2029's SEK 23.3; 27.70x that is SEK 646; adding the FY2026 and FY2027 dividends (SEK 29.5) gives SEK 675, which is +77.5% on SEK 380.2.

Of that +77.5%, the roll of forward EPS from SEK 20.9 to SEK 23.3 contributes +11%, dividends +7.7%, and the multiple rising from 18.2x to 27.7x +52.6%. Three-quarters of the summary's return is therefore a re-rating to the "mania" band. The three-year column takes forward EPS to about SEK 26.3 (a blend of FY2030 and an extrapolated FY2031) and adds three dividends.

The re-based decomposition, from SEK 360.1. The table below applies the same mechanics to today's price of SEK 360.1 and today's forward EPS of SEK 20.9 at 17.25x, with FY2029 EPS of SEK 23.3 at end-2027, forward EPS of about SEK 26.3 at mid-2029, and dividends counted when paid (SEK 14.3 by end-2027; SEK 45.8 by mid-2029).

What drives the return.

  • The earnings leg is worth 12% to 26%, and it is the most dependable part. It is the base case's 7% to 9% a year of EPS compounding, with no help from growth above consensus, and it rests on the volume lines.
  • The dividend leg is a dependable 4% a year. It is paid at a 75% payout, rises with EPS, and is backed by a leverage ratio that no longer binds.
  • The multiple leg is the swing. At the current multiple the shares return 13% a year, an acceptable floor case for a compounder with a 40% return on equity. At my fair multiple they return 18% to 25% a year. The guideline's return needs the market to call 2027 the start of a new growth leg rather than a stalling year.
  • Nothing in the return depends on Denmark, Sigma, a buyback or a second hike; each is upside to it.

The probability-weighted return to end-2027 is about +25%. The base case (50%) returns +30%. The bull case (25%), with the EPS path 11% higher and a 21x multiple, returns about +55%. The bear case (25%), with the EPS path 20% lower and a 15.9x multiple, returns about -14% (a share price near SEK 300 plus one dividend). That gives a one-in-four chance of a double-digit loss over the period and a three-in-four chance of a gain above 30%. The asymmetry is the quantitative form of the memo's conclusion: the fundamental skew is positive, and the timing of entry is what sets the realised return.

Where I differ from the market. The sell-side's median target of SEK 430 (+19%) equals my 18-month base at the current multiple plus a dividend, which implies that the market is at about 18.5x FY2029 earnings and 20.6x its own too-high 2027 estimates. The market's return and mine differ through my lower 2027 earnings and my slightly higher multiple; the two differences net to the same place by end-2027, with more downside protection in mine.

What would change my view. Anything that changes the fair multiple (#11); and, on the earnings leg, the FY2027 range of outcomes (#9), since a 2027 outturn of SEK 16.2 would take FY2029 forward EPS down 15% to 20% with it.

Score: 65. A 13% a year floor return at the current multiple and 18% to 25% a year at a fair one, with a 25% probability of a double-digit loss over 14 months: better than most European financials trading at a bottom-quartile multiple, and below what the guideline's return implies.

#13. Summary conclusion on the business and the investment case

Avanza's quality is not in question; its rate of converting assets into earnings has just reset lower, in a sector that the market prices as a loser from falling rates and risk-off markets.

For the next two reports, the case is about estimates catching up with the Q3 run rate: a 2% to 4% cut to FY2027 EPS and a 1.3-point margin disappointment in 2027. The share price, at a fair trough band, has largely discounted that.

From the spring of 2027, the case is about four things the estimates do not carry as positives: an asymmetric rate lever with a conservative pass-through in the base; a leverage ratio turning from constraint to option; an unpriced Danish launch; and a cost cap that restores operating leverage from 2030.

The numbers: the base case is a 9% EPS compounder with a 4% yield at 17x two-year-forward earnings. The fair multiple is 19.5x now and 21x once the turn is evidenced. The return is 13% a year with no re-rating and 18% to 25% a year with a fair one.

The skews: the probability of guidance upgrades is nil by construction; the probability of sell-side upgrades is low for six months and rising thereafter; and the fundamental outcomes are skewed modestly positive over 12 to 24 months.

The verdict for Richard: Avanza today does not offer the unusually positive skew that Richard's framework hunts for. It becomes one if the January and April reports show income per customer holding above SEK 2,100, and both dates are known.

C

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: C. The rate turn and the Danish option are real but modest and dated beyond six months, the deposit internalisation is already in the base, and the near-term change force in estimates is negative.

B

Foundations' Robustness: B. A top-decile franchise with returns above 40%, cash earnings, a cost line met four years running and a volume engine disclosed monthly, held back from A by a 44% transactional revenue base and a revenue margin the moat does not protect.

C

Setups' Fit/Crispness: C. The closest fit is the setup of a cause for concern (yield conversion and rate dependence) in a high-quality business on a bottom-quartile multiple, leading to reversion to normal. But the business is medium-cyclical rather than low-cyclical, and the concern has not yet cleared in the estimates, so the setup is recognisable but not crisp until after 22 January 2027.

B

Case Riskiness: B. Few drivers, all visible in advance, no balance-sheet or franchise risk, and a floor multiple that has held; marked below A by 1.45x operating leverage on transactional revenue and a one-standard-deviation EPS range of plus or minus 10%.

NII is net interest income; AT1 is Additional Tier 1 capital; STIBOR is the Stockholm Interbank Offered Rate; ISK is the Swedish investment savings account; FSA is the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority; DPS is dividend per share; bp is basis points.
